title: Developer Relay: Rapid SDK Adoption Pilot & Cycle Tracker
creator: Arielle Chen
body:
Summary:
Run a concentrated adoption pilot ("Developer Relay") to validate a compact SDK + quickstart experience that reduces time-to-first-call and improves initial retention for new developer sign-ups. This ticket tracks the cycle-level plan, acceptance criteria, experiment design, and rollout milestones for the pilot across JS and Python SDKs, docs, and two quickstart templates (chat + embeddings).

Goals / success metrics:
- Time-to-first-call (TTFC) for new sign-ups: reduce median from ~18 minutes to <=8 minutes within pilot users.
- 7-day activation retention: increase by +15 percentage points for pilot cohort vs baseline.
- Quickstart completion rate (start -> successful first response): >= 70% for JS and Python templates.
- Bugs / blocking issues: P0 regressions <= 1 during canary.

Scope:
- Deliver "compact" quickstarts: minimal code + copy, one-click deploy example (Cloud Shell + Docker), and a guided interactive tutorial in Console for JS and Python.
- Docs: single-page quickstart (1 pager) + troubleshooting FAQ + versioned compatibility matrix.
- SDK: bundle lightweight helpers for auth, retries, streaming helper for chat, and a small sample app.
- Instrumentation: track event funnel (signup -> doc view -> clone/run quickstart -> first successful API call).

Key decisions / trade-offs made so far:
- Prioritize JS and Python before adding Go/Rust. Rationale: current signup telemetry shows 74% of new developer activity in these languages. (Trade-off: we delay niche language coverage but accelerate impact.)
- Use a "compact" quickstart (opinionated defaults) rather than a full-featured sample to optimize TTFC. If we see high support friction, we will iterate with more variants.
- Console-guided tutorial will be a lightweight overlay (no heavy Console engineering) for MVP; long-term we plan an embedded stepper.

Acceptance criteria for Pilot -> Canary -> GA:
- Pilot: internal beta with 50+ real customers (SEs + early paying teams), instrumented funnel, and qualitative feedback collected.
- Canary: 500 sign-ups routed to the new quickstart flow with rollback policy; telemetry shows TTFC target met and no major regressions.
- GA: rollout to all new sign-ups, rollout monitoring dashboards and playbook for support.

Artifacts & links:
- PRD: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1DevRelayPRD (spec + user journeys)
- Quickstart drafts: https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstarts/dev-relay (internal preview)
- GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev-relay-quickstarts (repo with sample apps and scripts)
- Console prototype design: https://www.figma.com/file/Console-Relay (mockups)

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Quickstart increases support load due to environment issues. Mitigation: include a self-diagnose script and expanded FAQ in MVP. Also add a telemetry filter to identify failing environments quickly.
- Risk: Changes to SDK surface create backwards incompatibilities. Mitigation: ship helpers as a namespaced additive package and include compatibility tests in CI (ENG-1842).

Next steps (this cycle):
1) Deliver JS + Python quickstart repo skeleton and console overlay prototype (owner: Mateo) — target: 2025-03-15.
2) Instrument funnel events with analytics team and create monitoring dashboard (owner: PM analytics) — target: 2025-03-22.
3) Run internal pilot with Solutions Engineering and two partner teams; capture qualitative interviews (owner: Arielle) — target: 2025-03-29.
4) Execute canary rollout plan (owner: Release Eng + PM) — target: 2025-04-08.

Support requests from other teams:
- Design (DES-221): required microcopy review and accessibility pass for quickstart snippets.
- Engineering (ENG-1842): CI job for compatibility tests & lightweight CLI packaging.

Notes for reviewers:
- The plan intentionally reduces surface area to accelerate shipping. We welcome feedback on whether we should include a third sample (serverless deploy) in MVP.
- Cost estimate: incremental infra cost for canary expected < $2k for the cycle (CDN + ephemeral compute).

Contact: Mateo Alvarez (pm) / Arielle Chen (lead PM)
updates: 2025-02-03: Kickoff meeting with Eng, Design, Analytics. Agreed on metrics and JS/Python prioritization. Action: Eng to prototype streaming helper by 2025-02-14.
2025-02-12: Design posted initial microcopy and accessibility checklist (DES-221). Minor copy adjustments requested for code examples (clarify auth flow).
2025-02-21: ENG spike completed. Prototype helper shows 40% reduction in example code size. Raised compatibility test gap (ENG-1842) — estimate 3 points to add CI job.
2025-02-28: Analytics schema v1 approved. Instrumentation events: doc_view, quickstart_clone, quickstart_run, first_success, support_ticket_created. Dashboard template created in Looker.
2025-03-04: Internal pilot sign-ups seeded (Solutions Eng + 3 partner teams). First qualitative interview scheduled 2025-03-06.
2025-03-08: Decision: proceed with canary after pilot if TTFC target achieved for >=60% of pilot cohort. Preparing canary rollout playbook and rollback triggers.
